Subject: [ALERT] SwiftCart eu-west-1 — GenAPI throughput drop

Team,

Monitoring just alerted: GenAPI endpoint serving SwiftCart (account swft_prod, eu-west-1) is showing a ~55% sustained throughput reduction starting 09:05 PDT with queue growth and a p95 token latency jump from ~420ms to ~2.1s. Errors are still within normal bounds but requests are queuing at the routing layer.

Initial data:
- Alert: https://alerts.redwood.ai/12345678
- Short traces attached: svc_routing_trace_0630.json
- Impacting key customers: SwiftCart (primary) — high request volume for checkout personalization.

Ask: can engineering confirm whether this is a runtime scheduling/regression or upstream traffic surge? If we need to take a canary rollback or route SwiftCart to a fallback variant, call it out. Also need a customer-facing note we can send through CS.

David
SRE — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-30T09:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] SwiftCart eu-west-1 — GenAPI throughput drop

Triage notes (quick):
- Root-cause hypothesis: a scheduler kernel tweak deployed in release 2028.06.29 caused suboptimal token-kv-affinity for long-context requests; with SwiftCart's heavy checkout bursts we see replica saturation and queueing at the routing layer.
- Evidence: sustained queue depth on node pool genapi-eu-3, hot threads pinned logging to kernel-sched path. Metric snapshots attached (hotspot-metrics-0630.png).
- Immediate mitigations available:
  1) Emergency rollback of scheduler kernel to 2028.06.27 (fast, ~8–12min if we have approval)
  2) Temporarily divert SwiftCart traffic to fallback model variant (slightly higher latency but stable) — requires routing change, ~20min to stage and validate
  3) Apply a short-term prefix throttling rule to smooth bursts — ~10min but may impact throughput for some of their requests.

Recommendation: rollback scheduler kernel to 2028.06.27 and then follow with a targeted rollout that ramps more conservatively. I will prepare the rollback patch (kernel-diff.patch attached).

If product wants a less invasive option we can divert to fallback while we validate rollback.

Ben
Engineering — Runtime Performance

[attachments: hotspot-metrics-0630.png, kernel-diff.patch]
